commit.message:
ci: persist golangci-lint analysis cache between runs

In this commit, we persist golangci-lint's per-file analysis cache in
the GitHub Actions cache store so the lint job stops re-typechecking the
whole repository from scratch on every run.

The lint targets bind mount ~/.cache/golangci-lint into the tools
container, but nothing persisted that directory between runs, so each job
started with an empty analysis cache ("File cache stats: 0 entries of
total size 0B" in the logs) and re-analyzed every package.

Every run restores the most recent snapshot, keyed by the lint config,
the tools module and the custom linter plugin sources, so a run never
reuses analysis results produced by a different linter. Only the nightly
master run saves a new snapshot: entries created by PR and merge queue
runs are only readable by that same PR and by master, and the repo's
shared cache space is already at its size limit. The save runs after
both lint steps and also when they failed, so the analysis that did run
isn't lost. A cancelled run saves nothing.

commit.message:
build: export the linter cache from the nightly run only

In this commit, we restrict the BuildKit cache export to the nightly
run and make export failures non-fatal.

The measured image export is roughly 650 MiB per run, because the GHA
backend exports the final image's layers including the Go toolchain base
layers, even with mode=min. Exporting on every PR push would therefore
fill the repo's shared cache store, which is already at its limit, and
evict the Go build caches that all jobs depend on. A PR-created cache
is only readable by that same PR and by master, so the writes mostly
help nobody. The nightly master run now writes the cache, and every
other run still reads it.

The export also gains ignore-error=true, so a cache service outage or
rate limit can't fail the lint job, and the build drops -q in favor of
--progress=plain so the logs show whether the cache was restored.

build: pin the new lint job actions by commit

In this commit, we pin both actions the lint job newly uses by their
commit hash rather than by their mutable major tag, matching how the
other workflows in this repo pin third-party actions. A moved tag can
otherwise change what a lint run executes without any review.

build: write the linter image cache on every CI run

In this commit, we drop the nightly-only gate on the linter image cache
export again.

The gate was keyed on the workflow_call tier input, which only exists in
the unmerged CI tiering stack; on this branch's base there is no nightly
caller at all, so the gate would have left the cache unwritten by anyone.
The cache is also useful per pull request: an entry saved by a PR is
restored by later pushes to that same PR, which is the common iterative
case.

To bound the shared cache space we export only the layers of the final
image (mode=min) instead of every intermediate layer, which skips the
unmodified golang base image layers that live in the public registry
anyway.

build: fix the custom linter cache wiring for CI

In this commit, we fix two problems in the previous iteration of the
linter build cache.

The gha cache backend reads its credentials from the ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN
and ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL environment variables, but those are not exposed
to plain run: steps by default. We add the crazy-max/ghaction-github-runtime
step to expose them before the lint steps, otherwise the cache import or
export fails inside the manually invoked docker build.

The docker-container driver that setup-buildx-action installs doesn't
load the built image into the docker image store by default, but the lint
targets run the image with docker run. We add --load so the tagged
lnd-tools image is available to the lint steps.

We also only export the cache from the nightly run (LINT_WRITE_CACHE),
since PR-created caches aren't readable by other PRs and would only
churn the shared cache store. PR and merge queue runs still read the
cache that the nightly run exports.

build: cache custom linter build in CI

In this commit, we make the tools Docker image build reuse a remote build
cache so the custom golangci-lint binary is no longer recompiled from
source on every lint run.

The lint job previously spent several minutes compiling the linter binary
on every cold runner, only for the next run to throw it away. We now set
up BuildKit with the GitHub Actions cache backend in the lint job, and
pass the cache configuration through a new DOCKER_BUILD_ARGS make
variable that is only populated when CI is set, so local builds keep
their existing behavior.

commit.message: docs: add release note for #11501

ci: skip matrix jobs at the job level outside their tier

The required matrix legs of unit-test, basic-integration-test,
cross-compile and dep-pin were kept instantiated in the pr and held
tiers and only skipped their steps, because a job-level condition is
evaluated before the matrix expands and a skipped matrix job never
reports the per-leg check names that the ruleset required. Every PR
push therefore occupied 13 runners for legs that did nothing, and a
held run 19.

Once CI result is the only required status check, those legs can be
skipped at the job level. The unit-test matrix is split into unit-test
(unit-cover and unit-module, all tiers) and unit-test-merge (the rest,
merge and nightly tiers) under the same name, so the check names stay
the same. basic-integration-test only runs in the merge and nightly
tiers, and cross-compile, unit-test and dep-pin skip at the job level
for documentation-only changes, drafts (cross-compile only) and held
runs.

CI result now lists unit-test-merge in its needs and tier lists, and
requires static-checks and lint in the pr tier. On pull requests it
lets the documentation-only and draft skips pass explicitly instead of
relying on step-level no-ops, and it requires check-commits on every
pull request run, so that the Check commits status check can be
dropped from the ruleset as well.

This must only merge after the ruleset requires CI result alone,
otherwise PRs wait forever for per-leg checks that are no longer
reported.

commit.message: docs: add release note for #11498

ci: hold CI on new pull requests until the ci-hold label is removed

Every new pull request starts a CI run right away, including draft PRs
that are still being worked on and PRs that will need substantial rework
or are closed without being merged. Together with the merge queue this
keeps the shared runners busy, and the runs of PRs that are actually
ready wait in line behind them.

Hold CI on new pull requests instead:

- The new ci-hold.yml adds the ci-hold label to every new PR. It runs
  on pull_request_target, so it can label PRs opened from forks, and
  never checks out or executes PR code.
- The CI gate of main.yml selects a new held tier while the label is
  present. All jobs skip (the required matrix legs stay instantiated
  and only skip their steps) and the CI result job fails, so a held PR
  can't enter the merge queue. Merge group and nightly runs are never
  held. Because the run for a newly opened PR starts at the same time
  as ci-hold.yml, the first attempt of an opened run is held even if
  the label isn't visible yet, unless it has already been removed again
  or the PR was opened with the GITHUB_TOKEN.
- Removing the label makes ci-hold.yml re-run the PR's latest CI run
  for its current head commit. The gate reads the labels from the API,
  so the re-run runs the pr tier, and its results are reported on the
  PR like those of the original run. Adding the full-ci label re-runs CI
  the same way. main.yml doesn't listen to label events itself, as
  every unrelated label change would cancel the run in progress.

The commit checks and the release notes checks now wait for the gate
job, as they have to know whether CI is held.
